chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'ah, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it permissible for a man to be breastfed by the Jewish woman, the Christian woman, and the polytheist woman? He said, 'There is no harm.' And he said, 'Prevent them from drinking wine.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a man become mahram to a Jewish or Christian woman through breastfeeding?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that breastfeeding by women of the People of the Book or polytheists is valid for establishing *mahram* kinship, reflecting the Shia view of the permissibility of *radha'* across religious boundaries. The specific condition to prevent them from drinking wine highlights the importance of physical and spiritual purity (*taharah*) in the nursing process, ensuring the milk remains suitable for creating the familial bond. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding family structures while maintaining ritual purity standards.
